title: Multiply Strings
prompt:
Given two non-negative integers as strings `num1` and `num2`, return their product as a string. No built-in big-integer conversion.

**Example**: `"123" × "456"` → `"56088"`.

Grade-school multiplication: digit `i` × digit `j` lands in result positions `i+j` and `i+j+1`.
hints: A product of an m-digit and n-digit number has at most m+n digits.
digit[i] × digit[j] contributes to positions i+j (carry) and i+j+1 (units) of the result array.
Accumulate, then skip leading zeros when building the string (but keep "0" itself).

solution.explanation: Multiplying digit i of num1 by digit j of num2 produces a value whose units land at result index i+j+1 and whose carry lands at i+j — a positional identity that lets you accumulate all partial products into one array without aligning shifts manually. A final pass drops leading zeros. O(m·n).
